cases.title: Added HandleContext to re-enter soft-rewritten Requests. (#709)
cases.bug: HandleContext resets the context (handlers and index) and re-enters routing without restoring them, so the original chain continues on the new route's handlers and middleware re-runs; it also returns c to the pool while still in use

matched.title: HandleContext returns the context to the pool while the caller still holds it
matched.failure: A handler calls engine.HandleContext(c) after rewriting c.Request.URL.Path. The nested call runs the target handlers and calls pool.Put(c). The handler returns, and ServeHTTP calls pool.Put(c) again. Two concurrent requests then call pool.Get and both receive the same *Context, so their writes and Params interleave.
notes: removed evidence that does not resolve: ref:gin.go:273

matched.title: Resetting and re-running the chain under an active Next() loop leaves the outer chain in an undefined state
matched.failure: A middleware at index 1 calls HandleContext to rewrite the path and then calls c.Next(). After HandleContext returns, the outer loop resumes at the index left by the inner chain, so the middleware's own post-processing and any handlers after it in the original chain are skipped or run against the new chain.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading confirmed the case but judged it trade off, not a defect (After the inner run, c.index and c.handlers belong to the replacement chain, so the outer Next loop resumes against that chain and the original chain's remaining handlers are skipped; this is deterministic, though it is an undocumented consequence of the re-entry design rather than a clear bug.)

matched.failure: A handler sets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and calls `res.send(body)` on an app with the default etag setting. Before this change the response carried an ETag, and a later conditional GET could get 304. After this change there is no ETag, so conditional requests always get a full 200 response.

cases.title: Add mergeParams option to Router

matched.title: Numeric merge mutates the parent's req.params object, which leaks child keys past the router
matched.failure: Mount a mergeParams router at '/user/id:(\\d+)' with a route '/*' and a handler after it. For /user/id:10/profile the outer req.params is {0:'10'} before the router. After the router runs, the outer object has been changed to include keys 1 and 2 from the child, so the handler after the router sees params it should not see. That is the case the 'restore req.params' change is meant to prevent.
